title:
Lahore Zoo & Safari
Engineering a Giant Naked-Eye 3D Anamorphic Wildlife Experience
metaTitle: Lahore Zoo 3D Anamorphic Billboard Animation | Elipse Studio
metaDescription: Engineering a naked-eye 3D anamorphic corner screen in Lahore—combining on-site viewpoint surveying, procedural brick VFX, dense SpeedTree foliage, and an 8K AI upscaling pipeline.
overviewHeading: Transforming an Urban Corner into an Open-Air Digital Safari
overviewText:
Lahore Zoo and Safari are historic cultural cornerstones. To re-energize public engagement ahead of seasonal tourism peaks, project leadership commissioned Elipse Studio to design a visual landmark that would stop moving city traffic and create a viral civic talking point.

Rather than broadcasting flat footage onto an outdoor LED screen, the Elipse Studio team engineered a forced-perspective 3D anamorphic optical illusion. By mathematically calibrating the 90-degree corner bend of the building's LED screen to the exact pedestrian viewpoint below, we created the optical sensation of an ancient architectural brick wall parting open to reveal a living, breathing jungle where a majestic leopard steps out of the forest and lunges into the open street air.
challengeHeading: Inside the Production Pipeline: How the Elipse Studio Team Built the Illusion
challengeText:
Most forced-perspective 3D animations fail because artists estimate angles from an office. If the virtual camera angle is off by just 5 degrees, the 3D depth collapses into a distorted blur on the street.

The Elipse Studio team traveled directly to Lahore for a multi-day residency while the screen scaffolding was under construction—conducting wildlife observational research at Lahore Safari, surveying pedestrian crossing paths, and locking the precise optical "sweet spot" coordinates before writing any 3D animation code.

title: Interactive Virtual Home | WebVR
metaTitle: Interactive Virtual Home: Unreal Engine Pixel Streaming | Elipse
metaDescription: Pioneering the transition from static 2D architectural renderings to browser-streamed real-time spatial exploration—engineered in Unreal Engine with dynamic daylight cycles, interactive material toggles, and sub-50ms WebRTC cloud streaming.
overviewHeading: Built When It Was Considered Impossible: The Benchmark That Launched Our Studio
overviewText:
Years ago, architectural pre-sales were locked inside a frustrating compromise: developers had to rely either on static 2D still renders or rigid, pre-rendered 360-degree panoramic "bubbles" where users clicked between fixed hotspots. Neither format allowed buyers to truly feel spatial volume, test daylight orientations, or freely walk unbuilt rooms.

Recognizing that the future of real estate lay in true real-time spatial computing, Elipse Studio engineered the Interactive Virtual Home as an internal R&D benchmark at a time when real-time architectural pixel streaming was virtually unknown in the commercial market.
challengeHeading: The Technical Benchmark That Won Dozens of Studio Contracts
challengeText:
Our objective was audacious: build a desktop-grade Unreal Engine luxury residence and stream it directly to standard web browsers over WebRTC with sub-50ms latency—requiring zero downloads, zero high-end gaming hardware, and zero technical friction.

The Commercial Result: This single project became the catalyst for Elipse Studio's exponential growth. By proving that real-time architectural immersion could run in any browser, this showcase earned the trust of global property developers and directly unlocked dozens of subsequent residential, resort, and commercial visualization contracts worldwide.

title: Volvo S90 Unreal Engine 5 Pixel Streaming Configurator
metaTitle: Volvo S90 Unreal Engine 5 Pixel Streaming Configurator | Elipse
metaDescription: Delivering showroom-grade photorealism directly to any web browser—combining native Unreal Engine 5 geometry, Lumen ray-traced reflections, and WebRTC Cloud Pixel Streaming with sub-50ms input latency and zero client-side hardware demands.
overviewHeading: Why Luxury Automotive Requires Cloud-Streamed Real-Time 3D
overviewText:
While lightweight browser-native WebGL is ideal for mass consumer goods (such as footwear or watches), high-ticket automotive retail demands uncompromising visual fidelity. An enterprise vehicle model contains millions of CAD polygons, intricate multi-layer metallic paint flakes, optical headlight refraction, and bespoke stitched leather textures that would choke standard smartphone processors and budget office laptops.

To demonstrate what is possible when automotive e-commerce moves beyond the graphical limitations of standard browser WebGL, Elipse Studio engineered this high-fidelity Volvo S90 configurator as an internal capability benchmark. Our objective: prove that a full Unreal Engine 5 desktop-tier application—complete with Nanite micro-polygons, dynamic Lumen global illumination, and multi-layer automotive clearcoat physics—can be streamed to any consumer smartphone or laptop via WebRTC with sub-50ms latency and zero hardware barriers.

title: KIA Sportage: Real-Time 3D Configurator
metaTitle: KIA Sportage: Real-Time 3D Configurator | Elipse Studio
metaDescription: Elipse Studio developed a high-performance, browser-based 3D configurator for the KIA Sportage using PlayCanvas. Running at 60 FPS across devices, it lets users customize paint finishes, explore a 360° interior, open doors, and switch lighting environments—all without cloud streaming costs.
overviewHeading: Balancing Photorealistic Vehicle Customization with Zero Server Streaming Fees
overviewText: Automakers and dealership networks face a challenging architectural choice when deploying digital 3D vehicle configurators. Server-rendered cloud streaming solutions (such as Unreal Engine Pixel Streaming) deliver ray-traced visuals but incur recurring cloud GPU costs of $0.03 to $0.08 per session minute. For high-volume automotive portals attracting hundreds of thousands of monthly car shoppers, cloud streaming bills quickly become cost-prohibitive. Conversely, low-fidelity 3D viewers often compromise on paint depth, reflections, and mobile frame rates. The challenge was to push client-side WebGL to its absolute graphical limit: creating a lightweight, sub-5 second loading 3D configurator for the KIA Sportage that runs natively inside mobile browsers at 60 FPS with zero cloud server costs.
challengeHeading: Interactive 360 Exploration Across Day, Night, and Studio Lighting
challengeText: Built entirely on the lightweight PlayCanvas WebGL engine, the KIA Sportage configurator gives buyers full interactive control over the exterior and interior. Switch seamlessly between three dynamic lighting environments: Studio (softbox showroom reflections highlighting metallic paint flakes), Day (natural outdoor sunlight with sharp ground shadows), and Night (toggleable LED headlights, DRLs, and taillights with ground light projection). Buyers can also click door handles for smooth animated opening, step inside for a 360-degree interior cockpit inspection, and swap factory paint colors and wheel rims instantaneously.
